summary: Dragomir Dimitrov works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA under Michael Hahn and a PhD from the University of Marburg by 2004, later holding posts at Marburg, the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.
Drodul Dorji Tenzin studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. His students included Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Ayu Khandro, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Drolma is a Tibetologist who earned an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo, where she studied under supervisor Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.
Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dudjom Rinpoche (1904–1987) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Jampal Delek Nyima, Min Ling Orgyen Namdrol Gyatso, and Pé Kö Lama Könchok Rabten, and taught numerous students, including Keith Dowman and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (1904–1987) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, founding the International Nyingma Society. He studied under teachers including Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Sera Khandro Dewé Dorje, and taught students including Matthew T. Kapstein and Alexander Berzin.

Duncan Ryūken Williams works in Buddhist, religious, and Japanese studies. After studying at Reed College and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi, he held posts at Harvard, UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Boston University in 2001 under the supervision of Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lobzang Trinle (1927–1997) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sera and Gyuto Monasteries. He served as professor at Minzu University of China and Tibet University, and held leadership roles at TASS and CTRC.

Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya (1899–1965) was an Indologist educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He held professorships at Narasinha Dutt College, Scottish Church College, Sanskrit College and University, and the University of Calcutta.
Durga Prasad Dikshit is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under R. K. Dikshit, Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi, and doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri.
Dwijendra Narayan Jha (1940–2021) was an Indologist and historian who pursued his studies at Presidency University, Patna University, and the University of Calcutta.
Dylan Esler works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from SOAS University of London and a PhD from KU Leuven by 2018, where he also held a post as a research scholar.

Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche works in Buddhist, religious, and Tibetan studies. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje, taught at Naropa University (1990), and founded Mangala Shri Bhuti.

Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University, he studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and directed the Nitartha Institute and Kamalashila Institute.

Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College and SOAS under teachers including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche, and founded Siddhartha's Intent, Khyentse Foundation, and Deer Park Institute.
Dániel Balogh is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology who has held posts at the British Museum (attested 2021) and Eötvös Loránd University (attested 2026).
